text: SOLUTION Given two continuous functions 0 < a(z) < b(z), we have 0 < flm a(z)de < flw b(z) dz, so if flm a(z) dz = oo (i.e, it diverges), then also flw b(z) de = oo (ie, it diverges). And if flm b(z) dz is finite (i.e, it converges), then also flm a(z) da is finite (i.e, it converges). But if flm a(z) dz is finite, all we know is that flw b(z) dz is at least as big, but it could be either finite or infinite (i.e., it could either converge or diverge). And if flm b(a:) dz = oo, all we know is that flw u(a:) dz is no bigger, but it could be either finite or infinite (i.e., it could either converge or diverge).
